title: Shopping and money
objectives: Ask and understand prices with magkano and piso
Buy things with bumili and pabili po, and pay with magbayad
Use quantities: kilo, dosena, piraso, bote
Bargain politely with tawad, and use ordinal numbers (una, pangalawa...)

grammar.title: Asking prices: magkano, piso — and a little bargaining
grammar.explanation:
Magkano means 'how much (money)'. Point it at anything: Magkano ito? — 'How much is this?' Magkano ang mangga? — 'How much are the mangoes?' Magkano po lahat? — 'How much is everything?'

The peso is piso in Tagalog: dalawampung piso = twenty pesos. In real markets you'll hear Spanish numbers for prices constantly: beinte (20), singkwenta (50), syento (100) — Beinte pesos po means the same as dalawampung piso. You don't need to produce these yet, but train your ear to catch beinte and singkwenta.

Mahal means expensive, mura means cheap. In a wet market (not a mall!) light bargaining is normal and friendly: Mahal naman po! May tawad po ba? — 'That's a bit expensive! Is there a discount?' Tawad is the haggled-off amount. The seller might answer: Sige, singkwenta na lang — 'Fine, just fifty then.'

examples.tl: Magkano po ito? — Limampung piso po.
examples.en: How much is this? — Fifty pesos.

examples.tl: Magkano po lahat? — Sandaang piso po.
examples.en: How much is everything? — One hundred pesos.

examples.tl: Mahal naman po! May tawad po ba?

examples.en: Vegetables are cheap at the market.

grammar.title: Buying and paying: bumili, magbayad, pabili po
grammar.explanation:
Bumili (to buy) is an -um- verb, so its three aspects follow Unit 7 exactly: bumili (bought), bumibili (buys / is buying), bibili (will buy). What you buy takes ng, where you buy takes sa: Bumili ako ng bigas sa palengke — 'I bought rice at the market.'

Magbayad (to pay) is a mag- verb: nagbayad (paid), nagbabayad (is paying), magbabayad (will pay). Nagbayad ako ng sandaang piso — 'I paid one hundred pesos.'

At a sari-sari store you don't browse — you call your order through the window with pabili po: Pabili po ng itlog! — 'I'd like to buy eggs, please!' It's the buying cousin of pahingi po from Unit 4. Money words to know when paying: pera (money), barya (coins/small change), sukli (the change you get back): May barya po ba kayo? Heto po ang sukli ninyo.

examples.tl: Bumili si Nanay ng isda kanina.
Bibili ako ng bagong sapatos bukas.
Heto po ang sukli ninyo — dalawampung piso.

grammar.title: Quantities: kilo, dosena, piraso, bote
grammar.explanation:
Market quantities follow one pattern: number + linker + measure + ng + thing. Isang kilo ng kamatis — 'one kilo of tomatoes.' Dalawang dosena ng itlog — 'two dozen eggs.' Tatlong piraso ng saging — 'three pieces of banana.' Isang bote ng tubig — 'one bottle of water.'

Piraso (piece) is the all-purpose counter when you just want a few of something: Pahingi po ng limang piraso — 'Five pieces, please.' Prices are often quoted per measure: Magkano po ang isang kilo? — 'How much per kilo?'

Small cultural note: bigas is uncooked rice (what you buy), kanin is cooked rice (what you eat, from Unit 4). Buy bigas, eat kanin — mixing them up is a classic learner slip Filipinos find charming.

examples.tl: Bumili kami ng dalawang dosena ng itlog.
Magkano po ang isang kilo ng bigas?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of rice?

examples.tl: Pabili po ng isang bote ng tubig.

grammar.title: Ordinal numbers: una, pangalawa, pangatlo...
grammar.explanation:
To say first, second, third, Tagalog puts pang- in front of the number, with small sound changes: una (first — a Spanish loan, the odd one out), pangalawa (second), pangatlo (third), pang-apat (fourth), panglima (fifth), pang-anim (sixth), and so on up: pampito, pangwalo... At A1, una to panglima cover almost everything you'll say.

They work like adjectives, linker and all: ang unang anak (the first child), ang pangalawang bahay (the second house). Ito ang unang araw ko sa Pilipinas — 'This is my first day in the Philippines.'

Handy shopping use: sa pangalawang tindahan — 'at the second store.' Mas mura sa pangalawang tindahan — 'It's cheaper at the second store' (mas + adjective = more/-er).

examples.tl: Nasa pangalawang mesa ang bag mo.
examples.en: Your bag is on the second table.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang saging sa pangalawang tindahan.
examples.en: The bananas are cheaper at the second store.

dialogue.title: At the fruit stall
dialogue.context: Kate practices her market Tagalog at Aling Cora's fruit stall. Ana watches, amused.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Magandang umaga po! Magkano po ang mangga?
lines.en: Good morning! How much are the mangoes?

lines.speaker: Aling Cora
lines.tl: Magandang umaga! Sandaang piso po ang isang kilo.
lines.en: Good morning! One hundred pesos a kilo.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Sandaan? Mahal naman po! May tawad po ba?
lines.en: A hundred? That's expensive! Any discount?

lines.speaker: Aling Cora
lines.tl: Ay, marunong ka na! Sige, nubenta na lang po.
lines.en: Oh, you already know how it works! Fine, just ninety.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Sige po. Isang kilo ng mangga at isang kilo ng saging.
lines.en: Alright. One kilo of mangoes and one kilo of bananas.

lines.speaker: Aling Cora
lines.tl: Ang saging, beinte pesos lang po ang isang kilo. Mura!
lines.en: The bananas are just twenty pesos a kilo. Cheap!

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Kate, bibili rin ako ng kamatis. Magkano po ang kamatis?
lines.en: Kate, I'll buy tomatoes too. How much are the tomatoes?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Isang kilo po. Magkano po lahat?
lines.en: One kilo, please. How much is everything?

lines.speaker: Aling Cora
lines.tl: Nubenta, beinte, singkwenta... Isang daan at animnapung piso po lahat.
lines.en: Ninety, twenty, fifty... One hundred sixty pesos for everything.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Heto po ang dalawang daan. May barya po ba kayo?
lines.en: Here's two hundred. Do you have change?

lines.speaker: Aling Cora
lines.tl: Mayroon po. Heto ang sukli ninyo — apatnapung piso. Salamat po, suki!
lines.en: I do. Here's your change — forty pesos. Thank you, dear customer!

exercises.prompt: How do you ask the price of something you're pointing at?
exercises.explain: Magkano asks specifically about price; ano asks what it is, nasaan where it is.

exercises.prompt: What is the opposite of mahal (expensive)?
exercises.explain: Mura = cheap. Mahal ang mangga, pero mura ang saging.

exercises.prompt: ___ po ang isang kilo ng bigas? (How much is a kilo of rice?)
exercises.explain: Magkano + ang + item asks its price; per-measure prices use isang kilo ng...

exercises.prompt: You're at a sari-sari store window and want two eggs. What do you call out?
exercises.explain: Pabili po ng + item is the set phrase for buying at a store window; pahingi is for asking to be handed something.

exercises.prompt: 'I bought fish at the market' — ___ ako ng isda sa palengke.
exercises.hint: The completed form of the -um- verb 'to buy'.
exercises.explain: Bili takes -um- after its first consonant for the completed aspect: b-um-ili = bought.

exercises.tl: Magkano po ito? — Singkwenta pesos po. — Ay, mahal! May tawad po ba?
choices: The buyer thinks 50 pesos is cheap and pays.
The buyer thinks 50 pesos is expensive and asks for a discount.
The buyer asks where the store is.
exercises.explain: Singkwenta = 50; the buyer says mahal (expensive) and asks May tawad po ba? — 'any discount?'

exercises.prompt: One kilo OF tomatoes: isang kilo ___ kamatis.
exercises.explain: Measures connect to their noun with ng: isang kilo ng kamatis, isang bote ng tubig.
Ordinals take pang-: pangatlo = third. Tatlo is plain 'three'; pangalawa and pang-apat are second and fourth.

exercises.prompt: I will buy one dozen eggs tomorrow.
exercises.answer: Bibili ako ng isang dosena ng itlog bukas.
accept: Bibili ako ng isang dosena ng itlog bukas
Bukas, bibili ako ng isang dosena ng itlog
Bibili ako bukas ng isang dosena ng itlog
exercises.explain: Future = contemplated bibili (no -um-); the quantity chains as isang dosena ng itlog.

exercises.tl: Heto po ang dalawang daang piso. — Salamat po. Heto ang sukli ninyo, singkwenta pesos.
exercises.prompt: How much change does the customer get?
exercises.explain: The customer hands over 200 (dalawang daan), and the vendor returns sukli of singkwenta — fifty pesos.

exercises.prompt: Mas mura ang gulay sa palengke, pero mas malapit ang tindahan sa kanto.
exercises.answer: Vegetables are cheaper at the market, but the store on the corner is closer.
accept: Vegetables are cheaper at the market, but the store on the corner is closer
The vegetables are cheaper at the market but the corner store is nearer
Vegetables are cheaper in the market, but the store at the corner is closer
exercises.explain: Mas + adjective makes a comparison: mas mura = cheaper, mas malapit = closer.

exercises.prompt: How much is everything? — One hundred pesos. Here's my payment.
exercises.answer: Magkano po lahat? — Sandaang piso po. Heto po ang bayad ko.
accept: Magkano po lahat? Sandaang piso po. Heto po ang bayad ko
Magkano lahat? Sandaang piso. Heto ang bayad ko
Magkano po lahat? Isang daang piso po. Heto po ang bayad ko
exercises.explain: Magkano po lahat totals the bill; sandaan (or isang daan) is 100; heto po hands something over politely.

exercises.prompt: Kate is the second child in her family. Which is correct?
exercises.explain: Pangalawa = second (ordinal); dalawa would just mean 'two'. The linker -ng joins it to anak through siya.
